Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.
A later successful build replaces the earlier one; do not assume automatic best-candidate
selection or rollback. Do not emit an unexecutable final revision after executions run out.

Reference inventory and parameterization:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps, and
uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Also record several reliable shared projection anchors distributed across the image:
long edges, intersections, repeated-size relationships, and major foreground cropping.
Distinguish observed edges from inferred geometry. Avoid false precision in uncertain bounds.
Map inventory items to named SceneAct assets with meaningful child parts. A valid hierarchy
verifies only emitted parts; it does not establish photographic completeness.
Do not invent hidden detail to fill uncertainty or discard a visible part solely for being small.

Keep camera parameters, layout, whole-object dimensions, component proportions and finishes
separately editable. Build reusable assemblies in a consistent local frame before placing
instances. Use explicit pivots for transforms when the default AABB center is inappropriate.
Do not rely on an empty group's origin being its geometry center. Preserve group membership,
semantic children and support relations through revisions and complexity reductions.

Fit projection, silhouette and coverage before microstructure. Use a compact complete first
scene, including all major visible content. Estimate camera pose and focal length jointly
from multiple anchors instead of fitting a single salient object. Check foreground cropping,
relative projected sizes, convergence and occlusion order together. Repeated objects provide
constraints but need not have identical visible silhouettes or perfectly regular placement.
For composite objects, estimate the overall silhouette, internal occupied space and gaps,
component aspect ratios, and visible underside or opening before adding repeated details.
An outer bounding box does not establish correct shape or internal coverage. Uniform size
and camera-ray distance changes cannot directly repair an intrinsic component aspect ratio.
A projected AABB is only a coarse correspondence aid, not a visible silhouette mask. Extreme
bounds may arise from near-plane crossings or behind-camera geometry; inspect the render
before treating them as evidence that geometry must be resized or deleted.

Rendered review and uncertainty:
Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving another available for correction.
After a render, compare against the original reference at full-image and local scales:
shared anchors and cropping; salient silhouettes, component proportions and gaps; visible
coverage and occlusion; broad brightness and material regions; then fine details.
Separate image evidence from priors about what the depicted objects usually look like.
Record a brief revision rationale in program comments: observed discrepancy, competing
explanations, selected parameter family, expected visible effect, and uncertainty.

When many independently placed anchors share an error, investigate camera/framing. When
anchors agree but one assembly differs, investigate its placement or shape. Neither pattern
proves a unique cause. Do not mandate a camera correction before every local correction, or
interpret every local error as geometry. Keep camera pitch, focal length, object distance,
whole-object scale and component proportions conceptually distinct. Avoid simultaneous,
unexplained changes to all of them. Prefer a small coherent correction supported by several
visible comparisons; retain already matching objects and uncertain alternatives.

If controlled observations or an executable module decision are supplied, use their actual
reported result rather than an earlier preferred hypothesis. An unresolved decision remains
unresolved: do not force a winning module from the sign of one score or nearly tied weights.
Measured interventions report appearance sensitivity under the tested conditions, not true
3D accuracy. A beneficial local scale response can compensate for camera or shape errors;
a harmful focal change rejects neither all camera explanations nor the opposite direction.
Do not extrapolate one tested magnitude or direction into a universal correction rule.
Only compare baseline-relative interventions when their baseline, reference region, metric
and rendering conditions are compatible. Preserve the reference region across comparisons;
do not move it with the edited object to improve a score. Inspect full-image and regional
changes separately when available, since a combined scalar can conceal damage elsewhere.
Predicted intervals are forecasts, not measurements or calibrated confidence intervals.
A forecast miss alone does not establish causal falsity. Untested interventions remain unknown.
An isolated-object image may clarify membership and silhouette, but replacing the background
confounds its similarity score; it does not justify removing the rest of the reconstruction.
Do not invent probe results or call APIs absent from the provided runtime.

Under unresolved attribution, prioritize reversible edits justified directly by visible
geometry and multiple anchors. Keep competing causes explicit, avoid speculative global
changes, and verify the resulting full scene if another execution is available. No change
is guaranteed to improve similarity. Render noise, lighting, occlusion and approximate
correspondence can confound comparisons. Do not model sampling noise as surface geometry.
Structural/material/composite checks establish their stated mechanical properties only.

The nominal solve budget is three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds;
use the runtime's remaining budget as authoritative. Reserve time for realization, the

helpers duplicate contents. Boolean operands incur mesh creation and modifier work.

as a planning heuristic, not a runtime guarantee or fixed count. Allocate complexity by
projected size, silhouette, openings, occlusion and confidence in the visible evidence.

silhouettes suffice, reserving fillet_box for visibly important rounding. Use a small reusable
material palette instead of distinct random materials for tiny primitives.
If execution times out without an image, report failed completion and leave the bottleneck

camera or appearance evidence. Reduced complexity alone is not verified success.

camera. Preserve material distinctions supported by the image. Check geometry and framing
before using lighting to compensate for silhouette errors; assess broad tonal regions before
adding texture. Do not globally overwrite materials merely to conceal a local mismatch.
If execution fails, use its actual traceback. A failed execution without an image supplies
no rendered visual feedback and does not justify unrelated camera or geometry changes.
Distinguish successful execution, available rendered review, mechanical validation and
measured visual improvement. Never claim a check was performed when its result is absent.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy, math, random

# Reference inventory (normalized image estimates):
# Ceiling .00-.99 x .00-.32: white narrow boards, hanging black pendants.
# Rear glazing .02-.73 x .31-.54; right glazing .72-1 x .25-.62.
# Tables and upholstered pedestal armchairs fill .00-.90 x .51-1.
# Large left pendant .02-.23 x .11-.40; large right pendant .72-.82 x .29-.40.
# Foreground chair back .00-.33 x .72-.91; tabletop cropped along bottom.
# Right palm .78-1 x .40-1, overlapping chairs, tables and windows.
# Observed anchors: rear window transom near y=.32; rear sill near y=.53;
# ceiling/right-wall junction rises toward upper right; chair feet grow strongly
# toward bottom; front tabletop and left chair are cropped. Exterior is uncertain.
# Asset map: room/{floor,ceiling,glazing}; pendant_*/{shade,neck,cable};
# dining_*/{table,chairs}; palms/{pot,trunk,fronds}; rear_planters.
# Geometry estimate: approximately 650 primitives, including 150 palm parts,
# 240 chair parts, 70 window/ceiling parts, and 50 lamp solids/cutters.
# Camera, furniture dimensions, component proportions and finishes are separate.

random.seed(13)
scene = Scene(name="Window cafe")
P = {
    "floor":(.24,.25,.23), "ceiling":(.87,.88,.84),
    "frame":(.27,.29,.27), "chair":(.32,.35,.31),
    "chair_edge":(.24,.27,.23), "table":(.46,.48,.43),
    "metal":(.58,.60,.56), "lamp":(.045,.065,.045),
    "leaf":(.055,.10,.055), "pot":(.20,.23,.19)
}
ROOM_W, ROOM_D, HEIGHT = 8.8, 12.6, 3.45
TABLE_W, TABLE_D, TABLE_H = 1.12, .83, .77
CHAIR_W, CHAIR_D = .72, .70

room=Asset(name="architecture")
scene.include("room",room)
room.include("floor",box((ROOM_W,ROOM_D,.12),(0,2.7,-.07),P["floor"]))
room.include("ceiling",box((ROOM_W,ROOM_D,.09),(0,2.7,HEIGHT+.045),P["ceiling"]))

# Narrow ceiling planks and faint longitudinal joints.
for i in range(49):
    y=-3.5+i*.26
    room.include("ceiling_joint_%02d"%i,
                 box((ROOM_W,.009,.006),(0,y,HEIGHT-.004),(.61,.63,.59)))
for x in [-3.5,-1.7,.1,1.9,3.7]:
    room.include("ceiling_seam_"+str(x),
                 box((.012,ROOM_D,.008),(x,2.7,HEIGHT-.006),(.72,.73,.69)))

# Flooring consists of dark rectangular tiles with pale narrow joints.
for i in range(25):
    x=-4.4+i*.37
    room.include("floor_long_%02d"%i,box((.009,12.6,.003),(x,2.7,.001),(.40,.42,.37)))
for i in range(35):
    y=-3.6+i*.37
    room.include("floor_cross_%02d"%i,box((8.8,.008,.003),(0,y,.002),(.36,.38,.33)))

# Bright exterior backing and low opaque window aprons.
room.include("rear_exterior",box((9.0,.08,3.6),(0,9.03,1.9),(.88,.91,.86)))
room.include("right_exterior",box((.08,13,3.6),(4.51,2.7,1.9),(.91,.93,.89)))
room.include("back_apron",box((8.8,.16,.72),(0,8.9,.36),(.69,.71,.66)))
room.include("right_apron",box((.16,12.6,.72),(4.4,2.7,.36),(.68,.70,.65)))
for z in [.76,3.12,3.40]:
    room.include("back_rail_"+str(z),box((8.8,.13,.065),(0,8.83,z),P["frame"]))
    room.include("side_rail_"+str(z),box((.13,12.6,.065),(4.32,2.7,z),P["frame"]))
for j,x in enumerate([-4.35,-2.65,-.95,.75,2.45,4.28]):
    room.include("back_mullion_"+str(j),box((.055,.13,2.65),(x,8.81,2.07),P["frame"]))
for j,y in enumerate([-3.5,-1.5,.5,2.5,4.5,6.5,8.85]):
    room.include("right_mullion_"+str(j),box((.13,.055,2.65),(4.29,y,2.07),P["frame"]))
room.include("left_window_post",box((.09,.16,2.7),(-4.34,8.8,2.05),P["frame"]))

# Soft, low contrast outside foliage and building bands.
outside=Asset(name="exterior_shapes")
scene.include("exterior",outside)
for i in range(22):
    x=random.uniform(-4.3,4.3)
    z=random.uniform(.9,1.8)
    shape=ball(random.uniform(.18,.39),(x,8.96,z),(.74,.79,.71))
    shape.resize((1,.22,1.1))
    outside.include("distant_foliage_"+str(i),shape)
outside.include("building_band",box((8.7,.03,.10),(0,8.95,1.03),(.78,.81,.76)))

def chair(name, px,py,angle=0):
    # Reusable local chair: front +Y, explicit floor pivot.
    a=Asset(name=name)
    a.include("foot",rod(.245,length=.045,center=(0,0,.035),color=P["metal"]))
    a.include("pedestal",rod(.075,length=.36,center=(0,0,.24),color=P["metal"]))
    a.include("seat_base",box((.73,.69,.12),(0,0,.46),P["chair_edge"]))
    a.include("seat_cushion",box((.65,.60,.085),(0,.015,.555),P["chair"]))
    a.include("back",box((.75,.115,.62),(0,-.31,.82),P["chair"]))
    a.include("back_top_edge",box((.76,.12,.025),(0,-.31,1.135),(.42,.44,.39)))
    for side in [-1,1]:
        a.include("arm_"+str(side),box((.085,.62,.32),(side*.36,.005,.73),P["chair"]))
        a.include("arm_cap_"+str(side),box((.09,.64,.025),(side*.36,.005,.90),(.41,.43,.38)))
    a.turn("z",angle,pivot=(0,0,0))
    a.move((px,py,0))
    return a

def table(name,x,y):
    a=Asset(name=name)
    a.include("top_edge",box((TABLE_W,TABLE_D,.045),(0,0,TABLE_H-.015),(.12,.15,.12)))
    a.include("top",box((TABLE_W-.018,TABLE_D-.018,.022),(0,0,TABLE_H+.015),P["table"]))
    a.include("column",rod(.065,length=.69,center=(0,0,.37),color=P["metal"]))
    a.include("base",rod(.265,length=.035,center=(0,0,.035),color=P["metal"]))
    # Small pale ashtray visible on several tables.
    a.include("ashtray",rod(.075,length=.018,center=(.18,.08,TABLE_H+.038),color=(.71,.73,.67)))
    a.move((x,y,0))
    return a

# Receding paired dining rows; modest irregularity reflects the photograph.
for row,y in enumerate([-.35,1.75,3.8,5.8,7.55]):
    for col,x in enumerate([-2.65,.25,2.85]):
        if row==0 and col==2:
            continue
        dining=Asset(name="dining_%d_%d"%(row,col))
        dining.include("table",table("table",x,y))
        dining.include("left_chair",chair("left_chair",x-.90,y, -90))
        dining.include("right_chair",chair("right_chair",x+.90,y,90))
        if row>=2:
            dining.include("far_chair",chair("far_chair",x,y+.77,180))
        scene.include(dining.name,dining)

# Foreground furniture creates the characteristic bottom and left cropping.
front=Asset(name="foreground_dining")
front.include("table",table("foreground_table",-2.45,-2.45))
front.include("rear_facing_chair",chair("large_cropped_back",-2.65,-1.65,180))
scene.include("foreground",front)
scene.include("right_foreground_chair",chair("right_foreground_chair",2.25,-.7,15))

def pendant(name,x,y,r=.30,bottom=2.40):
    a=Asset(name=name)
    # Hollow upper hemisphere gives a broad bell mouth and visible bright interior.
    dome=ball(r,(x,y,bottom),P["lamp"])
    dome.resize((1,1,.88),pivot=(x,y,bottom))
    inner=ball(r-.025,(x,y,bottom-.012),(.73,.75,.68))
    inner.resize((1,1,.88),pivot=(x,y,bottom-.012))
    lower=box((r*3,r*3,r*2),(x,y,bottom-r),P["lamp"])
    a.include("shade",subtract(dome,inner,lower))
    a.include("neck",rod(r*.35,length=r*.72,
                         center=(x,y,bottom+r*.91),color=P["lamp"]))
    a.include("neck_band",rod(r*.355,length=.032,
                              center=(x,y,bottom+r*1.08),color=(.40,.43,.36)))
    top=bottom+r*1.28
    a.include("cable",rod(.008,start=(x,y,top),end=(x,y,HEIGHT-.035),color=(.16,.18,.15)))
    a.include("ceiling_canopy",rod(.073,length=.02,center=(x,y,HEIGHT-.015),color=P["lamp"]))
    a.include("bulb",ball(.045,(x,y,bottom+.07),(.94,.94,.83)))
    scene.include(name,a)

pendant("large_left_pendant",-2.95,-1.6,.49,2.42)
pendant("large_right_pendant",2.35,2.10,.35,2.35)
pendant("middle_pendant",.15,3.10,.30,2.31)
pendant("rear_left_pendant",-2.55,4.55,.25,2.26)
pendant("rear_middle_pendant",-.55,6.3,.245,2.28)
pendant("rear_right_pendant",2.65,6.5,.23,2.3)
pendant("side_pendant",3.67,4.25,.23,2.30)
pendant("far_side_pendant",3.75,8.0,.22,2.30)
pendant("left_mid_pendant",-3.65,2.25,.27,2.26)

# A low row of planted dividers at the back.
planters=Asset(name="rear_planters")
scene.include("rear_planters",planters)
for i,x in enumerate([-1.8,-.7,.4,1.5]):
    planters.include("box_"+str(i),box((.90,.38,.40),(x,6.85,.75),(.35,.39,.32)))
    for j in range(7):
        xx=x+random.uniform(-.4,.4)
        yy=6.85+random.uniform(-.12,.12)
        h=random.uniform(.25,.55)
        planters.include("stem_%d_%d"%(i,j),
                         rod(.009,start=(xx,yy,.94),end=(xx+.09,yy, .94+h),color=P["leaf"]))
        leaf=ball(.105,(xx+.08,yy,.99+h),(.25,.31,.22))
        leaf.resize((1,.45,.5))
        planters.include("leaf_%d_%d"%(i,j),leaf)

# Right foreground palm, composed of individually editable stems and leaflets.
palm=Asset(name="right_palm")
scene.include("right_palm",palm)
px,py=3.43,-.20
palm.include("pot",rod(.31,length=.46,center=(px,py,.24),color=P["pot"]))
palm.include("pot_rim",rod(.335,length=.065,center=(px,py,.48),color=(.29,.32,.26)))
for k in range(10):
    angle=math.radians(-160+k*34)
    base=(px+random.uniform(-.13,.13),py+random.uniform(-.1,.1),.44)
    height=random.uniform(1.15,1.95)
    reach=random.uniform(.65,1.13)
    mid=(px+math.cos(angle)*reach*.40,py+math.sin(angle)*reach*.40,height+.10)
    end=(px+math.cos(angle)*reach,py+math.sin(angle)*reach,height-.08)
    palm.include("frond_stem_"+str(k),sweep_tube([base,mid,end],.014,P["leaf"]))
    for j in range(1,7):
        t=j/7
        cx=mid[0]+(end[0]-mid[0])*t
        cy=mid[1]+(end[1]-mid[1])*t
        cz=mid[2]+(end[2]-mid[2])*t
        length=.30*(1-t*.60)
        for side in [-1,1]:
            ex=cx+math.cos(angle+side*1.03)*length
            ey=cy+math.sin(angle+side*1.03)*length
            ez=cz+.13*(1-t)
            palm.include("leaflet_%d_%d_%d"%(k,j,side),
                         rod(.012,start=(cx,cy,cz),end=(ex,ey,ez),color=P["leaf"]))

realize(scene)

# Bright overcast windows with restrained interior contrast.
sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes=True
nodes=sc.world.node_tree.nodes
background=nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background=nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output=nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output=nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"],output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value=(.82,.85,.79,1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.65

area_emitter((0,8.3,2.6),power=1500,size=7,target=(0,1,.4),color=(1,1,.96))
area_emitter((4.0,2.8,2.7),power=1250,size=6,target=(-1,2,.8),color=(1,1,.96))
area_emitter((-2,-3,3.1),power=220,size=5,target=(0,3,1),color=(1,1,1))

# Joint framing estimate: wide view with substantial ceiling, rear sill at mid-height,
# foreground furniture cropped, and right window wall receding toward rear center.
set_view(position=(-.95,-5.0,1.74),target=(.25,5.0,1.67),
         lens=25.5,sensor=36)
sc.camera.data.clip_start=.08
sc.camera.data.clip_end=100
sc.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'
sc.view_settings.exposure=.45
sc.view_settings.gamma=1.0
# No rendering or saving: the external runner handles both.
```
